question: When does a KV-cache quantization method pay off for a given attention architecture?

notes: TRITON_ATTN is pinned for every primary arm. It is the only backend that validates for bfloat16, fp8 AND int4_per_token_head across all three models on SM80, SM90 and gfx90a, including GPT-OSS attention sinks. Pinning it removes the kernel confound: under default selection the backend changes with kv-cache-dtype (A100: bf16 -> FLASH_ATTN, fp8 -> FLASHINFER, turboquant -> TURBOQUANT).

Model WEIGHT precision is held at each checkpoint's native format and never swept. Only kv-cache-dtype varies. GPT-OSS-120B ships MXFP4 and cannot run BF16 weights on 4x40GB, so weight format differs BETWEEN models but is constant WITHIN a model. Cross-model comparison is therefore about attention architecture, not about weights.
max_model_len 49152 covers prefill_heavy (32768+256) and decode_heavy (1024+16384) with headroom, identically for every arm.

The decode-heavy regime uses LiveCodeBench under the Azure bursty trace, matching the existing scripts/performance/run_trace_azure_livecodebench_* contract. Synthetic fixed-length prompts were rejected: the natural length distribution is part of what the study observes.

Every arm runs with --reasoning-parser. bench.py sends thinking_token_budget only when --enable-thinking is set, and vLLM can only honour it with a reasoning parser configured -- without one the server returns 200 with empty content and zero decode iterations. Qwen uses 'qwen3' with explicit <think>/</think> delimiters; GPT-OSS uses 'openai_gptoss' (harmony channels, no delimiter config).

gptoss_120b.label: GPT-OSS-120B
gptoss_120b.notes: Sinks make TRITON_ATTN the only viable backend on SM80/gfx90a regardless of kv dtype; there is no second kernel to cross-check against.

kvtq4.notes: TurboQuant supports neither sinks nor sliding window, so GPT-OSS is structurally excluded. Different kernel from the primary arms: read it as a quantization-SCHEME comparison at 4 bits, never as a same-kernel dtype step.

decode_heavy.observes: KV growth per decode step, KV utilization, preemption, TPOT
decode_heavy.notes: LiveCodeBench is naturally decode-heavy: ~37 output tokens per input token, confirmed on the MI250 arms (ISL avg 602, OSL avg 22,670). Real prompts, not synthetic -- the request-length distribution is part of the workload.

prefill_heavy.observes: large one-shot KV allocation, KV write/read traffic, long-context retention
prefill_heavy.notes: Needs a real long-context dataset (candidates in the parent bench.py: mrcr, longproc, repobench). No runner yet.

sweep.refine: add points bracketing the observed saturation/preemption knee, i.e. around KV_capacity_tokens / (ISL+OSL)
